steps.what: Determine locations, boundaries and depths of cuts after inspecting the mine face

tasks.design: Keep determination of cutting limits with the operator using the mine plan and observed conditions. No model generates cutting coordinates or treats an assumed safety flag as permission to cut.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cutting limits depend on changing face conditions and the governing mine plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing survey marks and direct inspection support the task.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling observed conditions with the planned boundary and raising discrepancies.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can inspect the face and seek clarification before cutting.

reach.learn: Identify and escalate conflicts between plans and actual conditions

evidence.claim: Manual cutting-limit assessment is an E1 proposal; the supplied billing digest does not establish mining guidance capability.

assumptions: The baseline is on-site cutting-limit determination, not survey data preparation.
Survey staff produce marks through separate survey work; the operator inspects them and local conditions within s1 with all time retained.
No machine consumes a free structured cutting-authority or ground-safety field.
Existing plans and instructions suffice; no new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which plan discrepancies most often require supervisor clarification?

already_counted.description: Inspect conditions and determine cutting limits

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. No evidenced digital subtask is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe equipment for binding and malfunctions

steps.what: Observe and listen to equipment operation to detect binding, stoppage or malfunctions

tasks.design: Retain direct equipment observation and listening with the operator alongside existing machine indications. The proposal assumes no validated sensor classifier that replaces watchkeeping.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fault clues can depend on sound, movement and local operating context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instruments support direct observation without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Recognizing early faults amid normal changes in load and material.
tasks.human_edge: The operator combines sensory cues and can stop to investigate uncertainty.

reach.learn: Describe symptoms and operating context accurately

evidence.claim: Human equipment observation is an E1 design; the digest establishes no validated mining fault-detection replacement.

assumptions: The baseline is continuous observation, not entering a maintenance report.
The operator obtains sound and motion observations during s1 with all time retained; no malfunction label is assumed available beforehand.
Existing machine indications precede any new analytics system.
No new monitoring service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which failure modes have independently validated sensor indications at this site?

already_counted.description: Direct observation and recognition of equipment concerns

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving; no validated watchkeeping replacement is supplied.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Apply technologies intended to reduce mining environmental impact

steps.what: Apply approved technologies to minimize environmental impact under actual mining conditions

tasks.design: Keep practical application of approved technology with the operator and existing technical supervision. No specific technology or environmental benefit is invented from a digest about billing records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Applying a technology depends on equipment compatibility and local operating conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approved instructions support practical implementation.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether the application works as intended in this mine.
tasks.human_edge: The operator notices operating issues and escalates departures from instructions.

reach.learn: Separate intended benefits from measured site outcomes

evidence.claim: Manual practical technology application is an E1 proposal; no particular mining environmental technology is established by the supplied digest.

assumptions: The task applies already-approved technology, rather than selecting or procuring new equipment.
Technical staff produce approved instructions through the existing engineering process; the operator checks local conditions during s1 with all time retained.
No machine assumes a structured compatibility or environmental-benefit flag.
No new digital service or incremental upkeep is introduced; equipment investment cannot be estimated without a named technology.
research_questions: Which technology is being applied and what site measurement establishes its environmental effect?

already_counted.description: Practical application and observation of operating issues

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net saving zero. Environmental benefit is not assumed to be operator labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Guide and assist track and support crews

steps.what: Guide and assist crews laying track and resetting supports and blocking

tasks.design: Retain direct crew guidance and physical assistance with the operator. The work depends on the actual crew and support conditions, with no evidenced administrative stage to remove.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coordination depends on people and conditions at the worksite.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing work instructions and direct communication support the task.
tasks.still_hard: Maintaining shared understanding as positions and work conditions change.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can see the crew, clarify instructions and stop uncertain work.

reach.learn: Use clear signals and resolve conflicting instructions

evidence.claim: Manual crew guidance is an E1 proposal; the digest establishes no software replacement for this physical coordination task.

assumptions: The baseline is live guidance and assistance rather than preparing a crew roster.
The operator observes crew positions and work conditions within s1; all time remains counted without a free readiness field.
Existing instructions and communication suffice before software.
No new service or incremental upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: Which misunderstandings currently interrupt coordinated track or support work?

already_counted.description: Observe the crew, coordinate instructions and assist work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gives zero gross and net saving. No roster or reporting work is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Attentive mining operation and practical crew coordination
reach: Describe equipment symptoms to maintenance technicians
skills_to_grow: Distinguishing intended and measured technology benefits
role.ambitious_version: An operator who applies approved methods carefully and makes site concerns visible promptly
